query: What features can be extracted from a company's business description to predict its regional cluster?

per_column.name: dominant_industry
per_column.rationale: Industry categorization is a strong feature for predicting regional clusters and gives a genuine grouping axis. However groundedness is shaky: 23andMe (ancestry/health) tagged 'ai_ml' and 280 Group (product management training/consulting) tagged 'ai_ml' are unsupported by the source text, indicating misclassification for several rows.

per_column.name: description_length
per_column.rationale: Binned text length is exactly the kind of generic surface feature that adds little analytical leverage for predicting regional clusters. Values are trivially and correctly derivable from the text.

per_column.name: is_b2b
per_column.rationale: A B2B/B2C axis is a plausibly useful feature. But grounding is questionable: 280 Group (training/certification/consulting for enterprises) and 5AM Ventures / Accel (VC firms serving founders) are all labeled 'no', which seems inconsistent with clearly business-facing descriptions, suggesting unreliable labeling.

per_column.name: has_rd_focus
per_column.rationale: An R&D flag could help distinguish deep-tech clusters, but it is near-constant (6 of 199 'yes'), giving limited discriminative leverage. Sampled 'no' values are reasonable readings of the given descriptions.

per_column.name: tech_depth_score
per_column.rationale: A graded technical-depth signal offers a real modeling axis beyond a binary flag. It is heavily skewed toward 0 (137/199), reducing but not eliminating usefulness. Sampled values are defensible inferences from the text, though the scoring basis is not always transparent.

judge.rationale: The set contains genuinely useful axes for cluster prediction (dominant_industry, tech_depth_score, and to a degree is_b2b), but also weak or generic ones (description_length, near-constant has_rd_focus). Groundedness is undermined by observable misclassifications in the samples: 'ai_ml' assigned to an ancestry/health company and a product-management consultancy, and 'no' B2B labels for clearly business-facing firms. These indicate the categorical judgments are not consistently sound readings of the source text.
